Lukiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Lukiv's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1563, followed mainly Trisk Hasidism by the late 19th century and peaked at 2,337 people (60 percent of the town) in 1897. During WWI, refugees from Lutsk and Rozhyshche resettled in Lukiv, contributing to a lively cultural scene, including active drama circles. By 1941, the Jewish population had reached 2,621 (76 percent of the town). According to local residents, this cemetery once stood on the site of what is now a private orchard on Moleva Street; it was completely demolished by Soviet authorities after WWII.
